title: Schema conformance flight recorder for partial-stream and constrained-decoder edgecases
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a 'flight recorder' + automated test harness that captures partial streaming responses, decoder state snapshots, and model sampling context to validate JSON mode enforcement and constrained-decoder behavior across real-world edge cases. The recorder will be usable both as a debugging aid for customer incidents and as the canonical input dataset for deterministic compatibility tests and fuzzing campaigns.

Background: We continuously hit corner cases where streaming responses contain truncated JSON fragments, interleaved toolcall markers, or subtle schema drift that constrained decoders either mis-handle or silently accept. Existing test suites cover many happy-path streaming scenarios, but we lack a reproducible pipeline that (1) captures production-like token interleaving and decoder state, (2) replays them deterministically through the constrained-decoder shim, and (3) produces pass/fail plus granular compliance metrics to track regressions across runtime releases.

Scope & deliverables:
- Flight recorder service: lightweight token-level capture of streaming sessions (prefixes, partial tokens, toolcall boundaries, sampling temperature, model identifier, and KV-cache metadata). No PII should be captured; recorder will redaction-hook to strip user-provided payloads.
- Snapshot format: newline-delimited events (timestamp, stream-offset, token, sentinel-flag, decoder-state-hash) and a separate metadata manifest for model config and environment. Format must be stable and human-inspectable.
- Replay harness: deterministic playback into the constrained-decoder testing shim with configurable network conditions (drops, reordering, latency) and temperature/sampling overrides.
- Fuzz matrix: orchestrate sampling-temperature sweep, top-k/top-p variations, and random prefix corruption to surface failure modes.
- Compliance reporter: per-run JSON output with metrics (schema-violation-rate, partial-json-recovery-rate, toolcall-interference-count, fallback-invocations, decoder-assertions-triggered) and a summarized HTML dashboard for SRE/PM review.
- Integration points: console dashboards (rollout and regression views), PR gating check (optional), and a reproducible artifact uploaded to artifacts store for each failing run.

Non-goals: full production long-term storage of token payloads (recorder is for short-term retention only), changes to the runtime itself (this ticket builds the harness and tests; follow-up tickets will implement runtime fixes).

Privacy & security: recorder must implement a configurable redaction pipeline before writes. For initial rollout, recorder will run only in staging clusters with sampling of production traffic allowed under customer opt-in and explicit compliance review.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Operational notes: this harness will be used to triage two recent customer incidents: 1) intermittent schema truncation with lambda-cold-starts, 2) toolcall interleaving causing function-arg corruption. The flight recorder will supply the deterministic inputs for follow-up patches.

Implementation plan:
1) Define NDJSON schema and manifest format (2 days).
2) Implement recorder library and staging integration (3 days).
3) Implement replay harness + constrained-decoder shim wrapper (4 days).
4) Build fuzz matrix runner and reporting pipeline (3 days).
5) Wire into CI and dashboard (2 days).

Notes on robustness: replay harness should assert idempotency—replaying the same token sequence with identical decoder-state-hash must produce identical constrained-decoder outputs. In cases where sampling randomness causes divergence, the harness will run with a seeded RNG mode and fallback to exact matching or similarity thresholds.

Rationale for the flight recorder approach: capturing the token-level stream plus decoder state is the only reliable way to replicate streaming partial-JSON bugs that are timing-dependent or arise from interaction between batching, KV cache warm/cold, and quantization fallbacks. The recorder/harness approach reduces flakiness in our regression suite and provides artifacts for on-call debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Flight recorder writes NDJSON manifests and event files for streaming sessions and metadata manifest is validated against schema
Replay harness can deterministically replay 95% of recorded sessions in seeded mode; remaining 5% are flagged with divergence reasons
Fuzz matrix surfaces at least 3 new regression cases when run against runtime-1.25 with the constrained-decoder shim
Compliance reporter emits the required metrics and a per-run artifact saved to artifacts store for any failing run
Recorder redaction hook strips PII by default and staging runs demonstrate no sensitive payload in stored artifacts
test_plan: Create an initial corpus of 200 recorded sessions from staging including known incident traces. Run replay harness with seeded RNG, network-drop scenarios (0%, 1%, 5%), and temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7, 1.0). For each run capture schema-violation-rate, partial-json-recovery-rate, toolcall-interference-count, and fallback-invocations. Flag runs that exceed thresholds and create failing artifacts for engineering triage. Schedule nightly fuzz runs for 2 weeks and collect top-10 unique failure signatures for prioritization.
metrics_definitions: schema-violation-rate: fraction of replayed sessions where final parsed JSON fails schema validation
partial-json-recovery-rate: fraction of sessions where constrained-decoder recovered valid JSON from partial streams
toolcall-interference-count: number of runs where toolcall delimiters were misinterpreted or interleaved into JSON payload
fallback-invocations: count of constrained-decoder fallback-to-loose-mode during replay
replay-determinism-score: percentage of runs that match baseline output exactly in seeded mode
